_metadata.description: FBA inventory nexus posture by state. Captures whether FBA inventory storage creates sales tax physical nexus, with citations. This is a CPA research aid — postures reflect the best available interpretation, not legal advice.
_metadata.notes: Postures seeded from Avalara, Grant Thornton, Sales Tax Institute, and primary state authority. 'asserts' = majority position that FBA inventory creates nexus. 'carve_out' = state has marketplace facilitator carve-out that may shield seller. 'contested' = active litigation or conflicting guidance. 'unknown' = insufficient authority to determine.

AL.citation: Ala. Code § 40-23-68; Alabama DOR marketplace facilitator rules do not relieve seller of nexus from stored inventory.
AL.notes: Inventory in AL warehouses creates physical presence. Marketplace facilitator collection does not eliminate registration requirement.

AZ.citation: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 42-5043; Arizona TPT marketplace facilitator provision. Avalara guidance indicates FBA sellers shielded by MP provisions.
AZ.notes: Arizona marketplace facilitator law effectively carves out FBA-only sellers from registration obligation when Amazon collects.

AR.citation: Ark. Code § 26-52-117; Arkansas marketplace facilitator act. Grant Thornton 2024 summary: FBA inventory alone insufficient when MP collects.
AR.notes: Arkansas marketplace facilitator provisions may shield FBA-only sellers. Verify with DFA.

CA.citation: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 6203(c); CDTFA Publication 156. Inventory stored in CA creates nexus regardless of marketplace facilitator collection.
CA.notes: California clearly asserts that inventory stored in the state creates nexus. Also triggers $800 minimum LLC franchise tax under R&TC § 17941.

CO.citation: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 39-26-102(3); Colorado DOR guidance on physical presence. Inventory storage = physical presence.
CO.notes: Colorado treats stored inventory as physical presence. Marketplace facilitator collection does not eliminate seller registration.

CT.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 12-407(a)(15); Connecticut DRS marketplace facilitator guidance.
CT.notes: Connecticut treats inventory storage as establishing nexus. Marketplace facilitator provisions do not relieve seller nexus from physical presence.

FL.citation: Fla. Stat. § 212.06(2)(b); Florida DOR TAA 22A-013. Inventory stored in FL creates dealer status.
FL.notes: Florida treats inventory as establishing dealer nexus. Marketplace sales do not count toward seller's economic threshold, but physical presence from inventory is independent.

GA.citation: Ga. Code § 48-8-2(8)(M.1); Georgia DOR marketplace guidance. Inventory creates dealer status.
GA.notes: Georgia asserts that stored inventory creates nexus. Marketplace facilitator provisions apply to collection, not nexus elimination.

HI.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 237-13; Hawaii GET. No specific FBA inventory guidance found.
HI.notes: Hawaii uses General Excise Tax (GET), not traditional sales tax. FBA inventory nexus position unclear. No Amazon FCs currently in HI.

ID.citation: Idaho Code § 63-3611; Idaho State Tax Commission guidance on physical presence.
ID.notes: Idaho treats inventory storage as physical presence creating nexus.

IL.citation: 35 ILCS 105/2(1.1); Illinois Leveling the Playing Field Act. Avalara: IL marketplace facilitator law shields FBA sellers from separate registration when MP collects.
IL.notes: Illinois marketplace facilitator provisions effectively carve out FBA-only sellers. Inventory presence alone does not require separate seller registration when Amazon collects.

IN.citation: Ind. Code § 6-2.5-2-1(c); Indiana DOR marketplace facilitator guidance.
IN.notes: Indiana treats inventory as physical presence. Marketplace facilitator collection does not relieve seller from registration obligation arising from physical nexus.

IA.citation: Iowa Code § 423.14A; Iowa DOR marketplace facilitator rules. Avalara summary: FBA sellers shielded.
IA.notes: Iowa marketplace facilitator provisions may shield FBA-only sellers from separate registration. Verify with IDR.

KS.citation: Kan. Stat. § 79-3702(h); Kansas DOR guidance on retailer doing business.
KS.notes: Kansas treats inventory storage as doing business in the state, creating nexus.

KY.citation: Ky. Rev. Stat. § 139.340; Kentucky DOR marketplace facilitator guidance.
KY.notes: Kentucky treats stored inventory as physical presence. Recent FC openings increase exposure.

LA.citation: La. Rev. Stat. § 47:301(4)(m); Louisiana Sales Tax Commission guidance.
LA.notes: Louisiana treats inventory storage as dealer nexus. Complex local tax structure (parishes).

ME.citation: Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 36, § 1754-B; Maine Revenue Services. No specific FBA inventory guidance found.
ME.notes: Maine has no known Amazon FCs. FBA inventory nexus position not clearly established. Monitor if Amazon opens facilities.

MD.citation: Md. Code, Tax-Gen. § 11-701; Maryland Comptroller guidance. Home state — nexus from LLC formation regardless of inventory.
MD.notes: Maryland is home state. Nexus established by LLC formation. Inventory presence is secondary but also creates nexus.

MA.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 64H, § 1; Massachusetts DOR Directive 17-1. Inventory creates physical presence.
MA.notes: Massachusetts treats inventory stored in state as physical presence creating vendor nexus.

MI.citation: Mich. Comp. Laws § 205.52(1); Michigan Treasury marketplace facilitator guidance.
MI.notes: Michigan treats inventory as nexus-creating activity. Marketplace facilitator collection does not eliminate seller physical presence.

MN.citation: Minn. Stat. § 297A.66; Minnesota DOR Revenue Notice 19-02.
MN.notes: Minnesota treats inventory as physical presence. Also has economic nexus from transaction count.

MS.citation: Miss. Code § 27-67-3; Mississippi DOR guidance on doing business.
MS.notes: Mississippi treats inventory storage as doing business in the state.

MO.citation: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 144.605; Missouri DOR guidance effective Jan 2023.
MO.notes: Missouri began requiring sales tax collection in 2023. Inventory storage creates physical presence.

NE.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2701.13; Nebraska DOR guidance on retailer engaged in business.
NE.notes: Nebraska treats inventory as physical presence creating retailer nexus.

NV.citation: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 372A.200; Nevada Tax Commission marketplace facilitator guidance. Avalara: FBA sellers may be shielded.
NV.notes: Nevada marketplace facilitator provisions may shield FBA-only sellers. Also has Commerce Tax for gross revenue >$4M (unlikely for most small sellers).

NJ.citation: N.J. Stat. § 54:32B-2(i); New Jersey Division of Taxation TB-90. Inventory = physical presence.
NJ.notes: New Jersey clearly treats inventory storage as physical presence. High volume of Amazon FCs in NJ.

NM.citation: N.M. Stat. § 7-9-10; New Mexico TRD guidance on engaging in business.
NM.notes: New Mexico uses Gross Receipts Tax (not traditional sales tax). Inventory creates engaging-in-business nexus.

NY.citation: N.Y. Tax Law § 1101(b)(8); New York DTF TSB-M-19(2)S. Marketplace facilitator provisions. Avalara: FBA-only sellers may be relieved.
NY.notes: New York marketplace facilitator law may relieve FBA-only sellers from separate registration when marketplace collects. Economic nexus uses AND test ($500k AND 100 txn).

NC.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-164.8(b); North Carolina DOR marketplace facilitator guidance.
NC.notes: North Carolina treats inventory as physical presence. Approaching economic threshold.

ND.citation: N.D. Cent. Code § 57-39.2-02.2; North Dakota Tax Commissioner guidance. Avalara: FBA sellers may be shielded.
ND.notes: North Dakota marketplace facilitator provisions may shield FBA-only sellers from separate registration.

OH.citation: Ohio Rev. Code § 5741.01(H)(2); Ohio Department of Taxation Information Release ST 2019-02.
OH.notes: Ohio clearly asserts inventory creates nexus. Also has Commercial Activity Tax (CAT) for Ohio gross receipts >$150k.

OK.citation: Okla. Stat. tit. 68, § 1392.1; Oklahoma Tax Commission marketplace facilitator guidance. Avalara: FBA sellers may be shielded.
OK.notes: Oklahoma marketplace facilitator provisions may shield FBA-only sellers. Note: confirmed 3PL warehouse creates independent physical nexus regardless of FBA posture.

OR.citation: Oregon has no general sales tax. Or. Rev. Stat. § 320.
OR.notes: Oregon has no general sales tax. FBA inventory nexus is irrelevant for sales tax purposes. Some specific excise taxes exist.

PA.citation: Online Merchants Guild v. Hassell (M.D. Pa., filed 2023). 72 P.S. § 7201; Pennsylvania DOR REV-717.
PA.notes: CONTESTED. Active litigation (Online Merchants Guild v. Hassell) challenges whether FBA inventory storage creates nexus for out-of-state sellers when Amazon is the marketplace facilitator. Pennsylvania asserts nexus; industry groups contest. CPA must independently evaluate.

RI.citation: R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-18-15; Rhode Island Division of Taxation guidance.
RI.notes: Rhode Island treats inventory storage as physical presence.

SC.citation: S.C. Code § 12-36-70; South Carolina DOR Revenue Ruling 19-3.
SC.notes: South Carolina treats inventory as physical presence creating nexus.

SD.citation: S.D. Codified Laws § 10-45-1; South Dakota DOR guidance. Post-Wayfair nexus includes physical presence from inventory.
SD.notes: South Dakota treats inventory storage as physical presence.

TN.citation: Tenn. Code § 67-6-102; Tennessee DOR Important Notice 19-18.
TN.notes: Tennessee treats inventory as physical presence. Also has franchise & excise tax implications.

TX.citation: Tex. Tax Code § 151.0242; Texas Comptroller Rule 3.286. Marketplace facilitator provisions. However, franchise tax (Tex. Tax Code Ch. 171) still applies.
TX.notes: Texas marketplace facilitator provisions may shield FBA-only sellers from SALES TAX registration. HOWEVER: Texas franchise tax applies independently — must file No Tax Due report + PIF annually if doing business in TX. Dual obligation.

UT.citation: Utah Code § 59-12-107(2); Utah State Tax Commission guidance.
UT.notes: Utah treats inventory storage as physical presence creating nexus.

VA.citation: Va. Code § 58.1-612; Virginia Tax marketplace facilitator guidance.
VA.notes: Virginia treats inventory as physical presence. Marketplace sales do NOT count toward seller's economic threshold.

VT.citation: Vt. Stat. tit. 32, § 9701; Vermont Department of Taxes. No specific FBA guidance found.
VT.notes: Vermont has no known Amazon FCs. FBA inventory nexus position unclear.

WA.citation: Wash. Rev. Code § 82.04.067; Washington DOR Special Notice. Inventory = substantial nexus.
WA.notes: Washington clearly asserts inventory creates nexus. Also has B&O tax on gross receipts — separate from sales tax. Dual obligation.

WI.citation: Wis. Stat. § 77.51(13g); Wisconsin DOR marketplace facilitator guidance.
WI.notes: Wisconsin treats inventory storage as physical presence.

WV.citation: W. Va. Code § 11-15A-1; West Virginia State Tax Dept. No specific FBA guidance found.
WV.notes: West Virginia has no known Amazon FCs. Economic nexus may exist from sales volume. FBA inventory position unclear.

WY.citation: Wyo. Stat. § 39-15-101; Wyoming DOR. No specific FBA guidance found.
WY.notes: Wyoming has no known Amazon FCs. FBA inventory nexus position unclear.

DC.citation: D.C. Code § 47-2001; DC OTR. No specific FBA guidance found.
DC.notes: DC has no known Amazon FCs. FBA inventory nexus position unclear.

DE.citation: Delaware has no general sales tax.
DE.notes: Delaware has no general sales tax. FBA inventory nexus irrelevant for sales tax. Some gross receipts taxes exist.

MT.citation: Montana has no general sales tax.
MT.notes: Montana has no general sales tax. FBA nexus irrelevant for sales tax.

NH.citation: New Hampshire has no general sales tax.
NH.notes: New Hampshire has no general sales tax. FBA nexus irrelevant for sales tax.
